source: I want a racing game with a city and a dealership

image_prompt.text: A wide starting grid of evenly spaced slots across the street where cars line up side by side
Barriers along the street edges - kerbs, rails and blocked side roads - that physically keep cars on the route
A hairpin section of the circuit forcing a clean direction reversal
a car dealership with a glass showroom and cars parked outside, sitting on the circuit near the start
a city the route runs through - buildings lining both sides of the street, sidewalks and street lighting

layout_placement.text: Starting grid slots at the line
Lap and split detection at the line and at key turns, to count laps and catch cars cutting the course

notes: Prompt does not say whether the city is a closed circuit or a free-roam map you also race in. Read as a circuit, because 'racing game' with no other qualifier means a lap route and Racing's own boundary rule sends a no-lap driving map to Simulation instead.

The dealership is a building you go into to buy a car. Racing has no notion of a hub, a garage, or anything you do between races, so it is carried as free text on the circuit rather than as an option.

open_questions.ask: A closed street circuit with laps, or a free-roam city you can drive anywhere in?
Is the dealership somewhere you walk into and buy cars, or just a landmark on the route?
How much city - a few blocks around the track, or a whole drivable city?

theme: Modern Urban - contemporary city streets, asphalt and concrete

coverage_missing.ask: Laps around a circuit, or point-to-point races through an open city?
Is the dealership functional - do you go in and buy cars with race winnings?
How long should a lap be?
Daytime city, or neon night streets?

answers.ask: A closed street circuit with laps, or a free-roam city you can drive anywhere in?
answers.answer: Use a closed street circuit with laps.

answers.ask: Is the dealership somewhere you walk into and buy cars, or just a landmark on the route?
answers.answer: The dealership should be somewhere players can walk into and buy cars.

answers.ask: How much city - a few blocks around the track, or a whole drivable city?
answers.answer: Keep it to a few city blocks around the track so the game stays focused and playable.
